transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Since that freeway crash about three weeks ago, I feel constantly on edge, like I’m scanning for danger all the time and can’t relax, especially when I’m out driving. It's just making it really hard to get through my normal routine.

Since the crash, have you been having unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about it, or mostly just feeling generally worried and tense? Also, are you avoiding reminders like driving or the freeway?

Yes, during the day I'll suddenly see the injured driver's bloody face and hear the crunch of metal, and at night I keep waking up from half-dreams of screeching brakes. I've also been completely avoiding the freeway, even rearranging my work schedule to take side streets because driving makes me feel so incredibly tense and on guard.
Have these symptoms been going on continuously for more than one month since the crash, or has it only been about three weeks so far? If they’ve changed over time, when did they start?

No, it hasn't been a month yet—it's been exactly three weeks since the crash. All of this started the very next day and hasn't let up at all, and honestly, it feels like it's been much longer because of how exhausting it is.
Since the crash, have there been any periods of at least a day or two when these symptoms mostly went away, or have they been present almost continuously the whole three weeks?

No, there haven't been any breaks at all. It has been pretty much continuous for the entire three weeks, and I haven't had a single day where things felt back to normal. I've just been constantly on edge without any real relief.

Just to clarify, are your symptoms still ongoing right now, and if they continue, will it soon be more than one month since the crash? That timing helps me tell whether this fits an acute stress reaction or post-traumatic stress disorder.

Yes, they are still happening every single day and haven't gotten any better. Since the crash was three weeks ago, if this keeps up for another week, it will be a full month. Right now, it doesn't feel like it's letting up at all.
Before this crash, had you ever experienced a similar traumatic event that caused the same kinds of symptoms for more than a month? Or is all of this only tied to this crash three weeks ago?

No, I've never gone through anything like this before, and I've never had these kinds of symptoms in the past. This is all completely new to me and only started after that freeway crash three weeks ago.

Have these symptoms now lasted longer than one full month since the crash, or is it still under a month? If they have passed one month, are the nightmares, intrusive memories, avoidance, and feeling on guard still happening?

No, it is still under a month; it has been exactly three weeks since the crash. All of these symptoms, like the bad sleep, the flashes of the crash, and feeling constantly on edge, are still happening very actively right now.

Have you had any moments during the crash or afterward where you felt detached, numb, dazed, or like things weren’t real? That can help me tell whether this is more of an acute stress reaction versus symptoms that may develop into PTSD.

Yes, I’ve felt really numb and disconnected from everything lately. For example, at my kid's soccer game, everyone was cheering but I just felt completely flat, like I was watching it on TV rather than actually being there. I just couldn't feel any real joy about it.

Did that detached or unreal feeling start right during the crash or immediately afterward, and has it been happening repeatedly since then? Or is it more just a general emotional numbness that developed later?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact moment it started or if I felt that way during the actual crash itself. Lately, though, I just feel this flat, disconnected numbness—like I'm watching my life on TV rather than actually being there—and I can't seem to feel any real happiness or joy.
Since the crash, have you had times when things felt unreal or dreamlike, or you felt outside your body watching yourself? Or is it mainly emotional numbness without that unreal/out-of-body feeling?

It’s really a mix of both. I feel completely numb and unable to feel any real joy, but I also have this strange feeling of being disconnected and watching my own life happen from the outside, almost like I'm watching a TV show instead of actually being there.

Right during the crash or in the minutes immediately after, did you feel dazed, like things weren’t real, or as if you were outside your body? Or did that disconnected feeling only start later in the days after the crash?

It’s really hard to tell if I felt that way during the crash because I have big memory blanks from that night and can't recall chunks of what happened. But that disconnected feeling—like I'm just watching things on TV instead of being there—is definitely happening now, like when I felt completely flat and couldn't feel any joy at my kid's soccer game.

In the crash itself or immediately afterward, do you clearly remember feeling dazed, numb, like things weren’t real, or as if you were outside your body? Or did those disconnected feelings only begin later in the days after the accident?

I honestly don't clearly remember how I felt in the immediate moments during or right after the crash because there are big chunks of that night that are just a blank to me. I only know for sure that I've been noticing that disconnected, flat feeling later on in the days and weeks since it happened.

Besides the memory gaps, in the moments during or right after the crash did you clearly feel dazed, like the world wasn’t real, or like you were outside your body? Or did those experiences only start later in the days after the accident?
I don't really recall feeling dazed or like I was outside my body at the time of the crash. Besides the blank spots in my memory, I don't think I experienced those specific feelings back then.

Have these symptoms now continued past one full month since the crash, or is it still less than a month? If they have passed a month, are the nightmares, intrusive memories, avoidance, and feeling on edge still happening?

It is still less than a month; it has been about three weeks since the freeway pileup. All of these struggles—the bad sleep, the flashes of the crash, and being constantly on edge—have been happening consistently during this entire three-week period.

Just to confirm, have these symptoms now lasted more than one full month since the crash, or are they still only three weeks out? This timing is the main thing that separates acute stress disorder from PTSD.
No, it is definitely still under a month. It has been exactly three weeks since the crash, so the symptoms have been going on for just that long.
